8.3 — Player Attack: Fight Back

You have a swing animation and an axe. Today the swing stops being decoration: a click spawns a hitbox, the hitbox checks for enemies, and the boss's number goes DOWN. The combat loop — the sentence "I hit it, it hurt" — takes about ten lines.

Predict First ~10 min

Recall the player's attack animation from 1.6: mouse button 0 sets the Attack trigger. That trigger plays frames; frames convince nobody. The QUESTIONS to answer before writing code:

  • WHERE does the hitbox live when no attack is happening? (Not "hidden somewhere" — destroyed, or deactivated, or zero-sized. Pick one and say why.)
  • WHEN does damage happen — the instant of the click, or during part of the swing? (Real games: a window within the animation. Ours: a fixed window after the click — simpler, same contract.)
  • WHAT stops you from hitting the boss EVERY frame of the window? (You already own the answer: the 3.3 cooldown pattern — your swing has a fire rate, exactly like the turret.)

Socratic

The AP exam calls two-way interaction "input → program behavior → output." Write this fight as that sentence: input (___), behavior (___), output (___). Where does the OUTPUT become a new INPUT (the boss reacting)? That loop — you act, world answers — is what interactivity IS.

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — the hitbox. Child of the player: a GameObject named AttackHitbox with a Box Collider 2D, Is Trigger, sized to reach one tile in front (about 1.2 × 1). No Renderer. On the "Player" physics layer is fine — your 7.2 raycast masks mean the hitbox will never confuse the ground check (it is a trigger, and triggers are not what ground raycasts ask about).

Step 2 — the window + cooldown. In PlayerController, where the mouse-0 branch already sets the Attack trigger, add the damage window in the starter's voice:

[SerializeField] private float attackRange = 1.2f;
[SerializeField] private float attackCooldown = 0.8f;
private float lastAttackTime;

private void Update()
{
    if (Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0) && Time.time >= lastAttackTime + attackCooldown)
    {
        lastAttackTime = Time.time;
        animator.SetTrigger("Attack");   // your 1.6 line
        TryHitEnemies();
    }
}

private void TryHitEnemies()
{
    Collider2D[] hits = Physics2D.OverlapBoxAll(
        transform.position + (Vector3)(Vector2.right * facingDir * 0.7f),
        new Vector2(attackRange, 1f), 0f, enemyLayer);

    foreach (Collider2D hit in hits)
    {
        BossManager bm = hit.GetComponent<BossManager>();
        if (bm != null) bm.ChangeHealth(-1);
    }
}

facingDir is your 4.1 sign trick: 1 or −1, wherever you last read your horizontal input. If your swing should hit ALL directions (a spin), drop facingDir — your spec decides, code obeys.

Step 3 — wire the boss. The boss collider is on the enemyLayer (set it!). Click near the boss: the bar from 8.2 falls by one. YOU HAVE A FIGHT. Everything else this unit is tuning, phases, and drama.

Bug Hunt: The phantom swing

  1. Set attackCooldown to 0 and hold the mouse. How many hits per second does a held button deal — and why did the turret teach you to predict this (3.3)?
  2. OverlapBoxAll with the wrong layer mask (Everything). What else does your swing hit — pickups? Projectiles? What does the projectile's Ground-tag destroy teach you about collateral damage?
  3. The boss deals CONTACT damage (4.4 style) AND you must stand close to hit it. Play the range game: how many frames are you inside the boss's touch when you land your swing — and should the boss have a melee cooldown LONGER than your swing's (argue with numbers)?
  4. Hit the boss in PHASE 3 — does your attack still work? Why must damage-dealing be phase-INDEPENDENT (a hint: what did phase guards protect 8.2 from)?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Combat design

  1. Tune the range game: attackRange 1.2 vs. boss contact radius. Where does your 8.1 arithmetic land NOW — is the fight still 60–90 seconds? Adjust HP, not the range, until the pace matches the spec.
  2. Add hit FEEDBACK: the boss flashes white for 0.1s on taking a hit (a sprite tint swap). Why is "no reaction" the deadliest combat bug even when the numbers work?
  3. Commit + push: "8.3a: player melee + boss takes damage".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Build a trigger hitbox and a click window with a cooldown
  • Use OverlapBoxAll with a layer mask and facing direction
  • Connect the swing to BossManager.ChangeHealth and see the bar move
  • Tune the range game against the contact damage trade
